text: What if the ships simply stopped coming… and the only man left on your island became the monster?
Clipperton: a speck of coral more than a thousand kilometers from Acapulco. In the early nineteen hundreds, Mexican soldiers and their families lived there, under Captain Rah-mohn Ar-no.
text0: Clipperton: a speck of coral more than a thousand kilometers from Acapulco. In the early 1900s, Mexican soldiers and their families lived there, under Captain Ramón Arnaud.

text: They depended on supply ships. Then, as revolution tore through Mexico, the ships stopped coming. Food ran out. Scurvy spread.
When a ship appeared on the horizon, Ar-no and the last soldiers rowed out to reach it. They never came back.
text0: When a ship appeared on the horizon, Arnaud and the last soldiers rowed out to reach it. They never came back.

text: Only one grown man was left among the women and children: the lighthouse keeper, Victoriano Al-vah-rez. He declared himself king of Clipperton.
text0: Only one grown man was left among the women and children: the lighthouse keeper, Victoriano Álvarez. He declared himself king of Clipperton.

text: Survivors described rape, beatings, and murder. There was nowhere to run. Beyond the beach, there was only ocean.
On July eighteenth, nineteen seventeen, Alicia Ar-no and Teer-sah Ren-dohn killed him.
text0: On July 18, 1917, Alicia Arnaud and Tirza Rendón killed him.

text: That same day, the U. S. S. Yorktown appeared on a wartime patrol. It hadn't come for them. Eleven survivors went home. Help arrived the very day they stopped waiting for it. This is Plot Twist, with A. and R.
